compiled_standalone_kernel_resources.scope: Static standalone test executable declarations; not measured occupancy or a claim about every compiled production kernel.

implementation: Each64-element input or weight block stores8 bytes: its maximum encoded exponent, nonzero count and eight six-bit counts below maximum minus0/2/4/6/8/10/12/14. Counts exclude zeros; each stored strict-below count is at most63. A requested threshold rounds upward to a stored threshold, preserving an upper count. For any split ea>=cut and eb>=target-cut, their sum cannot fall below target; the union of the two lower-exponent sets therefore bounds potentially inexact BF16 products for arbitrary operand correlation. The minimum of eight such union bounds stays conservative. The current coarse bound supplies an upper magnitude for every interior K16 carry. Products with summed unbiased exponent at least maximum minus11 have exact alignment. Replace64 possible product losses per C64 block with the bounded count, retaining four carry losses and four times four normalization units, every outward rounding step, and the unchanged conditional native2^-19 coefficient. Original zero-C WMMA instructions, explicit FP32 additions, center values, candidate compaction and staged2 replay remain unchanged.
correctness_scope: Host ASan/UBSan checks all65536 payloads, complete histogram thresholds, union bounds, and393216 canonical prefix endpoints under three simulated native-error profiles. Every counted actual original product loss is covered. Native generated cases check every summary word, identical raw matrix centers, non-widening errors, complete candidate permutations and independent CPU endpoints, including zeros, unsupported rows and partial C64 tails. Full captured projection attempts check every final BF16 output against GB10, every selected raw FP32 replay and every coarse interval against an independently generated complete canonical output. Original coarse center/error arrays are comparison-only, and no reference is a candidate input. All prepared encodings, metadata, immutable inputs, guards and unused index/metadata storage are checked after every attempt. QKV repeats1023 original input/reference rows; OUT repeats1023 inputs and uses its already8192-row GB10 reference. No real-model token loop is run.
timing_scope: Three variants rotate through one warmup and three measured attempts: current hipBLASLt QKV heuristic4 or OUT heuristic0 plus original L2 selection/staged2 replay, original C64 envelope, and exponent-count C64 envelope. Completed host clocks include full lossless operand preparation, matrix producer, norm/eligibility preparation, new metadata preparation where used, candidate compaction, host count read and exact replay. The same metadata allocations exist in all arms; controls must leave them untouched. Allocation, reset, reference generation, copies and verification are outside clocks. Component results do not measure TTFT or decode throughput.
numerical_limit: The retained native2^-19 coefficient remains conditional; finite host and GPU comparisons do not prove a universal hardware bound.
decision: Keep the exponent-count route isolated and preserve the tested product control. Every captured BF16 output and selected original raw replay matches, but the q8192 component complete QKV route is214.192ms versus169.299ms for original C64 and59.3921ms for current matrix/L2; OUT is121.9ms versus102.175ms for retained C64. The tighter count removes1636897/594348 candidates relative to C64, while preparation/producer/selection grows enough to outweigh the saved replay. This is a component regression, not a product performance result. The first OUT attempt was rejected by an omitted test-entry allowlist flag before tensor loading; the one-line guard repair was rebuilt and both complete projection routes were rerun. Continue structural work against the completed retained-control profile, with all numerical and product gates unchanged.
